text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale hit Lebanon on Wednesday but there was no immediate report of damage or casualties.
Beirut residents in the fifth floor of an office building felt the tremor at 7.55 p.m. (1755 GMT). A reporter in the northern port of Tripoli said buildings there shook for about 20 seconds.

"The earthquake which measured 5.7 on the Richter scale had its epicentre 323 km (200 miles) northwest of the observatory of Bhannes -- 25 km (15 miles) north of Beirut", Seismologist Charles Thabet said.
"It was in the direction of Cyprus and was followed by two or three aftershocks with lower magnitude," he added.
There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.
In Turkey, Anatolian news agency said two earthquakes measuring 3.8 and 5.5 on the open-ended Richter scale shook southern Turkey on Wednesday evening, damaging a number of houses.
Residents in Cyprus's capital Nicosia said they felt the ground shake around 1800 GMT.
